t1.title: Ways of travelling to work in one city, 1990 and 2020
t1.p: The chart below shows the percentage of workers using different ways of travelling to work in one European city in 1990 and 2020. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
t1.pv: Biểu đồ cho thấy tỉ lệ người đi làm bằng các phương tiện ở một thành phố châu Âu năm 1990 và 2020. Tóm tắt đặc điểm chính và so sánh.
t1.m:
The bar chart compares the proportion of workers in a European city who used five different ways of getting to work in 1990 and 2020.

Overall, the car remained the most common way of commuting in both years, but its share fell considerably, while train and bicycle use roughly doubled.

In 1990, just over half of all workers (52%) drove to work. Buses were the second most popular option at 18%, followed by walking at 12%. Only 10% of commuters took the train and 8% cycled.

By 2020, the proportion travelling by car had dropped to 38%. In contrast, train use more than doubled to 21%, making it the second most common method, and cycling also doubled, from 8% to 16%. The figures for buses and walking declined slightly, to 15% and 10% respectively.

In summary, although the car was still dominant, commuters in this city shifted noticeably towards trains and bicycles over the thirty-year period.

t1.title: Visitors to three museums, 2010–2025 (millions)
t1.p: The graph below shows the number of visitors to three museums in one city between 2010 and 2025. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
t1.pv: Đồ thị cho thấy số khách (triệu) tới ba bảo tàng ở một thành phố từ 2010 đến 2025. Tóm tắt đặc điểm chính và so sánh.
t1.m:
The line graph illustrates how many people visited three museums in one city from 2010 to 2025.

Overall, the Science Museum and the History Museum became more popular over the period, whereas visitor numbers at the Art Gallery declined. By 2025, the Science Museum had become the most visited of the three.

In 2010, the Art Gallery was the most popular attraction, with 2 million visitors, compared with 1.2 million for the Science Museum and only 0.8 million for the History Museum. The gallery's figure rose slightly to 2.1 million in 2015 but then fell steadily, reaching 1.6 million in 2025.

Meanwhile, the Science Museum grew continuously, overtaking the gallery shortly before 2020 and finishing at 2.4 million, double its original figure. The History Museum also increased gradually, to 1.1 million in 2020, before rising more quickly to 1.5 million by the end of the period, almost twice its 2010 level.

t1.title: Minutes per day spent on four activities, by age group
t1.p: The table below shows the average number of minutes per day that people in three age groups spent on four activities in one country. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
t1.pv: Bảng cho thấy số phút trung bình mỗi ngày ba nhóm tuổi dành cho bốn hoạt động. Tóm tắt đặc điểm chính và so sánh.
t1.m:
The table compares the average daily time that three age groups in one country spent on social media, television, reading and exercise.

Overall, younger people spent much more time on social media, whereas older people watched far more television. Reading took up the least time for every group.

The youngest group, aged 16 to 24, spent 150 minutes a day on social media, almost four times as much as those aged 45 to 64, who spent only 40 minutes. The middle group was in between, at 90 minutes. Television showed the opposite pattern: the oldest group watched 160 minutes daily, compared with 95 minutes for people aged 25 to 44 and just 60 minutes for the youngest.

As for the other activities, exercise time fell with age, from 45 minutes to 30 and then 25 minutes. Reading figures were low and fairly similar, ranging from 20 minutes for the middle group to 35 minutes for the oldest.

t1.title: Household spending in one country, 1980 and 2020 (%)
t1.p: The pie charts below show how households in one country spent their money in 1980 and 2020. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
t1.pv: Hai biểu đồ tròn cho thấy hộ gia đình ở một nước chi tiêu thế nào năm 1980 và 2020. Tóm tắt đặc điểm chính và so sánh.
t1.m:
The pie charts show the proportion of household spending that went on six categories in one country in 1980 and 2020.

Overall, housing replaced food as the largest area of spending, while the shares for food and clothing fell significantly.

In 1980, food accounted for the biggest share of household budgets at 30%, followed by housing at 22%. Transport and clothing each made up 12%, and leisure represented 10%. The remaining 14% was spent on other items.

By 2020, the picture had changed considerably. Housing costs rose to a third of all spending (33%), while the share spent on food almost halved, falling to 16%. Clothing also dropped by half, from 12% to 6%. In contrast, leisure increased from 10% to 15%, and transport and other items rose slightly, to 14% and 16% respectively. Taken together, these changes suggest that households were spending a smaller part of their income on basic needs such as food and clothes, but a much larger part on accommodation.

t1.title: Sources of electricity in one country, 2010 and 2025 (%)
t1.p: The chart below shows the sources of electricity in one country in 2010 and 2025. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
t1.pv: Biểu đồ cho thấy nguồn điện của một nước năm 2010 và 2025. Tóm tắt đặc điểm chính và so sánh.
t1.m:
The bar chart illustrates the percentage of electricity that one country generated from six different sources in 2010 and 2025.

Overall, there was a dramatic shift away from coal towards renewable sources, especially wind and solar power, over the fifteen-year period.

In 2010, coal was by far the most important source, producing 45% of the country's electricity. Gas provided a quarter, nuclear power 15% and hydroelectric power 9%. Wind and solar together contributed only 6%.

By 2025, coal's share had fallen to just 15%, a third of its earlier level. Gas became the largest single source at 30%. The most striking change was the growth of wind power, which rose fivefold to 25%, and solar, which increased from 1% to 14%. Meanwhile, nuclear and hydro both declined slightly, to 12% and 4% respectively. As a result, wind and solar together supplied 39% of the country's electricity in 2025, more than coal and nuclear combined.

t1.title: Unemployment rate in three regions, 2005–2025 (%)
t1.p: The graph below shows the unemployment rate in three regions of one country between 2005 and 2025. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
t1.pv: Đồ thị cho thấy tỉ lệ thất nghiệp ở ba vùng của một nước từ 2005 đến 2025. Tóm tắt đặc điểm chính và so sánh.
t1.m:
The line graph shows changes in the unemployment rate in three regions of one country from 2005 to 2025.

Overall, all three regions followed a similar pattern, with unemployment rising sharply until 2010 and then falling gradually. The Coast region had the highest rate throughout, while the South always had the lowest.

In 2005, unemployment stood at 8% on the Coast, 6% in the North and 4% in the South. Over the next five years, the rate increased in every region, peaking in 2010 at 12%, 9% and 7% respectively.

After 2010, the figures declined steadily. The Coast saw the largest fall, from 12% to 6% by 2025. The North dropped to 5%, slightly below its starting point, while the South returned to exactly 4%, the same level as in 2005. The gap between the highest and lowest regions therefore narrowed from 5 percentage points in 2010 to only 2 points at the end of the period.

t1.title: Hilltown village in 1995 and today
t1.p: The maps below show the village of Hilltown in 1995 and today. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
t1.pv: Hai bản đồ cho thấy làng Hilltown năm 1995 và hiện nay. Tóm tắt đặc điểm chính và so sánh.
t1.m:
The maps illustrate how the village of Hilltown has changed between 1995 and the present day.

Overall, the village has become far more developed and residential, with farmland giving way to housing and new facilities being added, although the main road, the river and the original houses have remained in place.

In 1995, the northern half of the village, above the main road, consisted mainly of farmland in the west and a large forest in the east. Since then, the farmland has been replaced by a housing estate, and the forest has been reduced in size, with its western edge cleared.

South of the main road, the small shop in the south-west has been demolished and a larger supermarket has been constructed on the same site. The row of houses in the centre has not changed. The most noticeable addition is a bridge, which has been built across the river in the south-east, connecting the village to the land on the other side. In contrast, the river itself and the road running from west to east through the village are exactly as they were in 1995.

t1.title: A university campus now and the planned changes
t1.p: The maps below show a university campus at present and the plans for its development. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
t1.pv: Hai bản đồ cho thấy khuôn viên một trường đại học hiện nay và kế hoạch phát triển. Tóm tắt đặc điểm chính và so sánh.
t1.m:
The maps compare the current layout of a university campus with the changes that are planned for the future.

Overall, the campus will become more focused on accommodation and indoor facilities, as the car park and part of the sports field are set to be replaced by new buildings, while the academic buildings will stay the same.

At present, the northern part of the campus contains the library in the north-west corner and a large car park beside it. Under the plans, the library will remain unchanged, but the car park will be removed and student housing will be built in its place.

In the southern half, the lecture halls in the west will not be altered. However, the sports field, which currently occupies the whole south-east area, will be reduced to around half its size, because a new sports centre is going to be constructed on its northern part. Finally, the small café in the south-west corner will be extended eastwards, roughly doubling in size. There is no indication in the plans of where cars will be parked once the car park has gone.

t1.title: Riverside town centre in 2000 and 2025
t1.p: The maps below show the centre of the town of Riverside in 2000 and 2025. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
t1.pv: Hai bản đồ cho thấy trung tâm thị trấn Riverside năm 2000 và 2025. Tóm tắt đặc điểm chính và so sánh.
t1.m:
The maps show the changes that took place in the centre of Riverside between 2000 and 2025.

Overall, the town centre changed from an industrial and car-based area into a more residential and leisure-oriented space, with the factory disappearing and the main street being closed to traffic.

In 2000, a large factory stood in the north-west of the centre. By 2025, it had been demolished and the site had been divided between a block of apartments on the western side and a small park to the east of it. The bus station in the north-east, however, remained in the same position throughout the period.

The High Street, which ran from west to east through the middle of the town, was converted into a pedestrian street. To the south of it, the shops on the western side were kept, while the empty land opposite them, in the south-east, was developed into a row of restaurants. The river along the southern edge of the town centre was unchanged, so the new restaurants were built facing the water.

t1.title: How glass bottles are recycled
t1.p: The diagram below shows how glass bottles are recycled. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features.
t1.pv: Sơ đồ cho thấy quy trình tái chế chai thuỷ tinh. Tóm tắt đặc điểm chính.
steps: Used bottles are put into collection points
Bottles are taken by lorry to a cleaning plant
Bottles are washed with high-pressure water
Glass is sorted by colour
Glass is crushed and melted in a furnace
Melted glass is shaped into new bottles
New bottles are filled and sent to shops
t1.m:
The diagram illustrates the process by which used glass bottles are recycled and turned into new ones.

Overall, there are seven stages in the process, beginning with the collection of used bottles and ending with new bottles being delivered to shops. The process is cyclical, because the new bottles can eventually be collected and recycled again.

First, used bottles are placed in special collection points by the public. They are then taken by lorry to a cleaning plant, where they are washed thoroughly with high-pressure water to remove any dirt and labels. After that, the glass is sorted according to its colour, so that clear, green and brown glass are kept separate.

In the next stage, the sorted glass is crushed into small pieces and melted in a furnace at a very high temperature. Once it has melted, the glass is shaped into new bottles using moulds. Finally, the new bottles are filled with products, such as drinks, and sent to shops, where they are sold to customers and the cycle can begin again.

t1.title: The life cycle of a frog
t1.p: The diagram below shows the life cycle of a frog. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features.
t1.pv: Sơ đồ cho thấy vòng đời của con ếch. Tóm tắt đặc điểm chính.
steps: An adult female lays eggs (frogspawn) in water
After about 10 days, tadpoles hatch from the eggs
Tadpoles breathe through gills and feed on plants
At around 6 weeks, back legs begin to grow
At around 9 weeks, front legs appear and the tail shrinks
At 12–16 weeks, a young frog leaves the water
After 2–3 years, it becomes an adult and can breed
t1.m:
The diagram shows the stages in the life cycle of a frog, from egg to adult.

Overall, the frog goes through seven main stages, changing from an egg that develops in water into an adult that lives mainly on land. The whole cycle takes between two and three years and then begins again when the adult breeds.

The cycle starts when an adult female lays a mass of eggs, known as frogspawn, in water. After approximately ten days, tadpoles hatch from these eggs. At this stage, the tadpoles live entirely in water, breathing through gills and feeding on plants.

The tadpoles then gradually change their shape. At about six weeks, their back legs begin to grow, and by around nine weeks their front legs have appeared while their tails have become shorter. Between twelve and sixteen weeks, the animal has developed into a young frog and leaves the water. Finally, after two to three years, it reaches adulthood and is able to breed, which means that the cycle is repeated.

t1.title: How rainwater is collected for drinking
t1.p: The diagram below shows how rainwater is collected and made safe for drinking. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features.
t1.pv: Sơ đồ cho thấy nước mưa được thu gom và xử lý để uống như thế nào. Tóm tắt đặc điểm chính.
steps: Rain falls on the roof
Water flows through pipes into a storage tank
Leaves and dirt are removed by a filter
Water is stored in an underground tank
Water is pumped to a treatment unit
Water is cleaned with chemicals and UV light
Clean water is piped to homes for drinking
t1.m:
The diagram illustrates how rainwater is collected and treated so that it can be used as drinking water.

Overall, the process consists of seven stages, which can be divided into collection, storage and treatment, beginning with rain falling on a roof and ending with clean water being supplied to homes.

At the start of the process, rain falls on the roof of a building. The water then flows through pipes towards a storage system, and on the way, leaves and dirt are removed by a filter. After this, the filtered water is kept in a large underground tank, where it is stored until it is needed.

In the next stage, the water is pumped from the tank to a treatment unit. There, it is cleaned with chemicals and then exposed to UV light in order to kill any remaining bacteria. Finally, once it has been treated, the clean water is piped to people's homes, where it is safe to drink. Unlike natural processes, this one depends on electricity for pumping and treatment.

gt1.p: You live in a flat and your neighbours have been making a lot of noise late at night. Write a letter to the building manager. In your letter: describe the problem; explain how it is affecting you; say what you would like the manager to do.
gt1.pv: Hàng xóm gây ồn đêm khuya. Viết thư cho quản lý toà nhà: tả vấn đề; nó ảnh hưởng bạn thế nào; muốn quản lý làm gì.
c: Đề nghị quản lý làm gì
gt1.m:
Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing to complain about the noise coming from the flat above mine, number 14, which has become a serious problem over the past month.

Almost every night, my neighbours play loud music and have guests until two or three in the morning. On several occasions I have also heard furniture being moved and people shouting in the corridor.

As a result, I have been unable to sleep properly. I start work at seven o'clock, so I am exhausted during the day and I am finding it very difficult to concentrate. I did knock on their door once to ask them politely to be quieter, but nothing has changed.

I would be grateful if you could speak to the residents and remind them of the building rules about noise after eleven at night. If the situation continues, I would also like to know what further steps can be taken.

Thank you for your help. I look forward to hearing from you.

Yours faithfully,
Nam Tran

gt1.p: A friend from another country is coming to visit your city for a week. Write a letter to your friend. In your letter: suggest where they could stay; describe some places they should visit; offer to help in some way.
gt1.pv: Một người bạn nước ngoài sắp tới thành phố bạn một tuần. Viết thư: gợi ý chỗ ở; tả vài nơi nên đi; đề nghị giúp.
gt1.m:
Dear Emma,

I'm so excited that you're finally coming to Hanoi next month! I've been thinking about your trip, so here are a few ideas.

As for where to stay, I'd suggest a small hotel in the Old Quarter. It's lively, everything is within walking distance and there are lots of good places to eat. If you'd prefer somewhere quieter, there are some lovely guest houses near West Lake.

There's plenty to see. You should definitely walk around Hoan Kiem Lake early in the morning, when people are doing exercise there. The Temple of Literature is beautiful, and the Museum of Ethnology is really interesting if you want to learn about Vietnam's different cultures. And of course, you have to try street food at the night market!

I'll be happy to pick you up from the airport, and I can take a day off work to show you around. Just send me your flight details.

Can't wait to see you!

Love,
Linh

gt1.p: You recently attended a training course at work, but you were not satisfied with it. Write a letter to your manager. In your letter: give details of the course; explain what was wrong with it; suggest how future courses could be improved.
gt1.pv: Bạn vừa dự khoá đào tạo ở chỗ làm nhưng không hài lòng. Viết thư cho quản lý: nêu chi tiết khoá học; điều gì chưa tốt; gợi ý cải thiện.
gt1.m:
Dear Ms Johnson,

I am writing to give you some feedback on the customer service training course that I attended last week, from Monday to Wednesday, at our head office.

The course was intended to help staff deal with difficult customers, and I was looking forward to it. Unfortunately, I was disappointed with several aspects. Firstly, most of the sessions consisted of the trainer reading from slides, so there was very little chance to practise. Secondly, the examples were mainly about shops, which are not very relevant to our work in a call centre. Finally, the room was too small for thirty people, and it was difficult to concentrate.

I would like to suggest a few improvements for future courses. It would be more useful to include role plays based on real calls, so that we can practise the skills we have learned. I also think that smaller groups of ten to fifteen people would make the sessions more interactive. If possible, it would be helpful to ask experienced team leaders to share their own advice.

I hope these suggestions are useful, and I would be happy to discuss them with you.

Yours sincerely,
Minh Le

gt1.p: You left a bag on a train last week. Write a letter to the railway company. In your letter: give details of your journey; describe the bag and its contents; say what you would like the company to do.
gt1.pv: Bạn để quên túi trên tàu tuần trước. Viết thư cho công ty đường sắt: chi tiết chuyến đi; tả túi và đồ bên trong; muốn công ty làm gì.
gt1.m:
Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing to ask for your help in finding a bag that I left on one of your trains last Friday, 24 October.

I travelled from Manchester Piccadilly to London Euston on the train which departed at 17:15. I was sitting in coach C, and I believe I left the bag on the luggage rack above my seat when I got off in London at around 19:30.

The bag is a medium-sized black leather backpack with a small red label on the front pocket. It contained a silver laptop, a blue folder of work documents, a phone charger and a book. The laptop is particularly important to me, as it contains files that I need for my job, and the documents are confidential.

I would be grateful if you could check whether the bag has been handed in to your lost property office. If it has been found, I would like to know how I can collect it or whether it could be sent to my home address. I am happy to pay any delivery costs. Please contact me by phone on 07700 900123 or by email at the address below.

Thank you in advance for your help.

Yours faithfully,
Thu Pham

gt1.p: You have recently joined a sports club. Write a letter to a friend. In your letter: describe the club; explain why you joined it; invite your friend to join you.
gt1.pv: Bạn vừa vào một câu lạc bộ thể thao. Viết thư cho bạn: tả câu lạc bộ; vì sao bạn vào; rủ bạn tham gia.
gt1.m:
Dear Sam,

How are you? It's been ages since I last wrote. I've got some exciting news: I've just joined a badminton club near my flat!

The club meets three evenings a week in a big sports centre with six courts. There are about forty members of all ages, and most of them are friendly and very welcoming. There's also a coach who gives free lessons to beginners on Tuesday evenings, which is perfect for me.

I decided to join because I'd been sitting at my desk all day and I wasn't getting any exercise. I was also feeling quite stressed at work, and I wanted to do something fun to switch off in the evenings. After just a month, I already feel fitter, and I'm sleeping much better too. It's also a great way to meet new people.

Why don't you come along with me? I know you used to play at school, so I'm sure you'd enjoy it. New members can have a free trial session, so you wouldn't have to pay anything at first. We could play together and go for a drink afterwards.

Let me know if you're interested. Hope to see you soon!

Best wishes,
Ha

gt1.p: You have seen an advertisement for a part-time job at a local museum. Write a letter to the museum. In your letter: say which job you are applying for; describe your relevant experience; explain when you are available.
gt1.pv: Bạn thấy quảng cáo việc bán thời gian ở bảo tàng địa phương. Viết thư: nói ứng tuyển việc nào; kinh nghiệm phù hợp; khi nào bạn rảnh.
gt1.m:
Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing to apply for the position of part-time visitor assistant, which was advertised on your museum's website last week.

I believe I have relevant experience for this role. For the past two years, I have worked part-time as a guide for a local tour company, taking groups of up to twenty tourists around the old town and explaining its history. This has given me confidence in speaking to the public and answering questions. Previously, I also worked in a bookshop, where I developed good customer service skills and learned to handle payments accurately. I speak English and French fluently, which I think would be useful for helping international visitors.

I am currently studying history at university, so I have a strong interest in your collections, especially the exhibition on the region's industrial past.

As for my availability, I am free every Saturday and Sunday, and on Monday and Thursday afternoons from two o'clock. I could start at the beginning of next month.

I enclose my CV and would be happy to attend an interview at your convenience.

Yours faithfully,
An Nguyen

t2.p: Some people believe that online learning will soon replace traditional classroom teaching. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
t2.pv: Có người tin học trực tuyến sẽ sớm thay thế lớp học truyền thống. Bạn đồng ý tới mức nào?
t2.m:
Over the past decade, and especially since the pandemic, online courses have become a normal part of education. Some people therefore argue that traditional classrooms will soon disappear. While I accept that online learning will continue to grow, I disagree that it will replace face-to-face teaching in the near future.

There are clear reasons why online learning is attractive. It is flexible, so students can study at their own pace and fit lessons around work or family commitments. It is also often cheaper, because learners do not need to travel or live near a university. For adults who want to gain a new skill, such as programming, a well-designed online course can be just as effective as a classroom.

However, schools and universities do much more than transfer information. In a classroom, teachers can notice immediately when a student is confused or losing interest and change their approach. Learners also develop social skills, such as working in teams and debating ideas, which are difficult to practise through a screen. In addition, many children lack a quiet place to study or a reliable internet connection at home, so a move to purely online teaching would widen the gap between rich and poor families.

In conclusion, online learning is a valuable tool that will become even more common, particularly for adult learners. Nevertheless, because of the human and social benefits of classroom teaching, I believe the most likely future is a combination of the two rather than a complete replacement, with technology supporting teachers instead of taking their place.

t2.p: Some people think that city centres should be closed to private cars, while others believe that this would cause too many problems. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
t2.pv: Có người cho rằng nên cấm xe riêng vào trung tâm thành phố, người khác cho rằng việc này gây quá nhiều vấn đề. Bàn cả hai quan điểm và nêu ý kiến của bạn.
t2.m:
Traffic congestion and air pollution have led some cities to consider banning private cars from their centres. Although this policy has drawbacks, I believe that its benefits outweigh them.

On the one hand, opponents argue that a ban would create serious difficulties. Shops and restaurants in the centre might lose customers who are used to driving, and some businesses could even close. People with disabilities, elderly residents and parents with young children may find it much harder to move around without a car. Critics also point out that traffic might simply move to the streets just outside the restricted area.

On the other hand, supporters claim that car-free centres are healthier and more pleasant places. Without cars, air quality improves and noise levels fall, so walking and cycling become safer and more attractive. Space that was used for roads and parking can be turned into parks, cafés and public squares. Several European cities that have reduced car access have found that the number of visitors to their centres actually increased.

In my opinion, closing city centres to private cars is a sensible policy, provided that it is introduced carefully. Good public transport, exceptions for disabled drivers and delivery vehicles, and car parks at the edge of the centre can solve most of the problems that critics mention. Cities could also start with a ban on certain days or in a small area, so that residents and businesses have time to adapt. In conclusion, while the concerns are understandable, a well-planned ban would make cities cleaner and more liveable.

t2.p: International tourism has grown rapidly in recent decades. Do the advantages of this development outweigh the disadvantages?
t2.pv: Du lịch quốc tế tăng nhanh mấy thập kỷ qua. Lợi ích có lớn hơn bất lợi không?
t2.m:
Over the last few decades, international travel has become cheaper and easier than ever, and millions of people now visit other countries every year. In my view, although this trend brings some serious problems, its advantages are greater.

The main benefit of international tourism is economic. In many countries, tourism creates jobs not only in hotels and restaurants but also in transport, farming and handicrafts. For example, small coastal towns in Vietnam and Thailand have grown rapidly because foreign visitors spend money there. Tourism also encourages understanding between cultures. When people travel, they meet others with different traditions and ways of life, which can reduce prejudice and make them more open-minded.

However, there are clear disadvantages. Popular destinations can become overcrowded, which damages historic sites and makes life difficult for local residents. In some cities, rents have risen sharply because flats are rented to tourists rather than to local families. Air travel also produces a large amount of carbon emissions, which contributes to climate change. In addition, some traditional customs are turned into shows for visitors and lose their original meaning.

Nevertheless, I believe these problems can be managed. Governments can limit visitor numbers at fragile sites, introduce tourist taxes to pay for maintenance, and encourage travel outside the busiest seasons. Such measures allow countries to keep the economic and cultural benefits while reducing the harm.

In conclusion, international tourism has both positive and negative effects, but because of the jobs and cultural exchange it brings, I believe its advantages outweigh its disadvantages, provided that it is carefully controlled.

t2.p: In many countries, the number of children who are overweight is increasing. What are the causes of this problem, and what measures could be taken to solve it?
t2.pv: Ở nhiều nước, số trẻ thừa cân đang tăng. Nguyên nhân là gì và có thể làm gì để giải quyết?
t2.m:
In many parts of the world, a growing proportion of children are overweight, which increases their risk of serious illnesses later in life. This essay will examine the main causes of this trend and suggest some possible solutions.

The first cause is diet. Processed food and sugary drinks are cheap, widely advertised and available almost everywhere, and many busy parents rely on them instead of cooking fresh meals. The second cause is a lack of physical activity. Children today spend far more time on phones, computers and televisions than previous generations, and in many cities there are few safe places for them to play outside. As a result, they consume more energy than they use.

Several measures could help to reverse this situation. Governments could introduce taxes on sugary drinks and restrict advertisements for unhealthy food aimed at children, as some countries have already done. Schools also have an important role: they can provide healthy lunches, teach basic cooking and nutrition, and make sure that every pupil takes part in sport or exercise each day. Finally, local authorities should create more parks and safe cycling routes so that being active becomes part of children's daily lives.

In conclusion, childhood obesity is mainly caused by unhealthy diets and inactive lifestyles. It can be tackled through a combination of government regulation, better education in schools and more opportunities for outdoor activity. However, these measures will only succeed if parents also set a good example at home, since children's habits are shaped mainly by their families.

t2.p: In many countries, people are living longer than ever before. What problems does this cause for society? How can these problems be reduced?
t2.pv: Ở nhiều nước, người ta sống lâu hơn bao giờ hết. Điều này gây vấn đề gì cho xã hội? Làm sao giảm bớt?
t2.m:
Thanks to better healthcare and living standards, people in many countries are living much longer than previous generations. While this is a great achievement, it also creates several problems for society. This essay will discuss these problems and suggest some ways to reduce them.

The first problem is financial. As the number of retired people grows, governments must spend more on pensions, while there are fewer workers paying taxes to support them. A second problem is the pressure on health and care services. Older people are more likely to suffer from long-term illnesses, so hospitals become crowded and the cost of care rises. Finally, many elderly people experience loneliness, especially when their children have moved to other cities for work.

Several measures could help to solve these problems. Firstly, governments could gradually raise the retirement age, since people now stay healthy for longer. For example, a number of European countries have already increased the age at which people receive a state pension. Secondly, more investment in preventive healthcare, such as regular check-ups and exercise programmes, would help older people to remain independent and reduce the need for expensive treatment later. Thirdly, local communities can organise clubs, volunteer work and part-time jobs for retired people, so that they stay active and connected to others.

In conclusion, an ageing population puts pressure on public finances, health services and family life. However, these problems can be reduced by extending working lives, focusing on prevention and helping older people to remain active members of society.

t2.p: Some people think that university education should be free for all students. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
t2.pv: Có người cho rằng đại học nên miễn phí cho mọi sinh viên. Bạn đồng ý tới mức nào?
t2.m:
In many countries, students must pay high fees to attend university, and some people argue that higher education should be free for everyone. I partly agree with this view: university should be free for students who cannot afford it, but I do not believe it should be completely free for all.

There are strong reasons to reduce the cost of university. Education benefits society as a whole, because graduates become doctors, engineers and teachers who serve the community. If fees are too high, talented young people from poor families may decide not to study, which is a waste of their ability. Moreover, many graduates in countries with high fees start their working lives with large debts, which can delay buying a home or starting a family.

On the other hand, making university free for everyone is extremely expensive. The money must come from taxes, which means that people who never went to university help to pay for the education of others, including students from wealthy families who could easily afford the fees. Free university may also encourage some students to choose courses without thinking carefully about their future, because there is no cost if they change their minds.

In my opinion, the best solution is a system in which fees depend on family income. For instance, students from low-income families could receive free tuition and grants for living costs, while richer families pay part of the cost. Loans that are repaid only when graduates earn above a certain salary are another fair option.

In conclusion, although I agree that cost should never prevent able students from going to university, I believe that free education for every student is neither fair nor affordable.

t2.p: Advertising aimed at children should be banned. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
t2.pv: Nên cấm quảng cáo nhắm vào trẻ em. Bạn đồng ý tới mức nào?
t2.m:
Children today are exposed to a huge number of advertisements on television, websites and social media. Some people think that companies should no longer be allowed to target young audiences with their marketing. I strongly agree with this view, for two main reasons.

Firstly, children are not able to understand adverts in the same way as adults. Young children often cannot tell the difference between a programme and an advert, and even older children may not realise that the purpose of an advert is to persuade them to buy something. Companies use bright colours, cartoon characters and free toys to attract them. For example, many fast-food restaurants offer toys with children's meals, which makes children want unhealthy food for reasons that have nothing to do with the food itself.

Secondly, advertising aimed at children puts pressure on parents and can harm family life. Children who see attractive products repeatedly often ask their parents to buy them, and families with little money may feel guilty when they cannot. Advertising can also make children believe that owning the latest toy, phone or brand of clothes is necessary to be happy or popular, which is a harmful message.

Some people argue that a ban would hurt companies and limit freedom of speech. However, businesses could still advertise to parents, who are able to make careful decisions about what their children need. Several countries have already restricted advertising to young children without serious economic damage.

In conclusion, because the young are easily influenced and marketing can encourage unhealthy habits and unnecessary spending, I believe that adverts which target them should be prohibited.

t2.p: Some people prefer to work for a large company, while others prefer to work for a small one. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
t2.pv: Có người thích làm cho công ty lớn, người khác thích công ty nhỏ. Bàn cả hai quan điểm và nêu ý kiến của bạn.
t2.m:
When choosing a job, some people prefer to work for a large company, while others would rather join a small one. Both options have clear advantages, and in my opinion the right choice depends largely on a person's stage in their career.

On the one hand, large companies offer several benefits. They usually pay higher salaries and provide better insurance, pension schemes and training programmes. Employees in big organisations also have more opportunities for promotion, because there are many departments and positions. In addition, working for a well-known company looks impressive on a CV, which can help people find good jobs later.

On the other hand, small companies have their own attractions. Because there are fewer employees, each person usually has more responsibility and can see the direct results of their work. Staff in small firms often learn a wider range of skills, since they may be involved in sales, planning and customer service at the same time. The atmosphere is also often friendlier, and managers are easier to talk to. For example, a friend of mine who works for a small design company says that she has learned more in two years than she would have in five years at a large firm.

In my view, small companies are a better choice for young people at the start of their careers, because they offer valuable experience and responsibility. Later, when workers have more family commitments, the security and benefits of a large company may become more important.

In conclusion, both large and small companies have advantages, and people should choose according to their personal goals and circumstances.

t2.p: More and more people now use smartphones to manage almost every part of their lives. Do the advantages of this outweigh the disadvantages?
t2.pv: Ngày càng nhiều người dùng điện thoại thông minh cho hầu hết mọi việc. Lợi có lớn hơn hại không?
t2.m:
Smartphones are now used for almost everything, from banking and shopping to studying and keeping in touch with friends. Although this development has some negative consequences, I believe that its advantages outweigh its disadvantages.

The most obvious advantage is convenience. With a smartphone, people can pay bills, book tickets and check information in seconds, without visiting an office or waiting in a queue. This saves a great deal of time. Smartphones also help people stay connected. For instance, families living in different countries can make free video calls every day, which was impossible only twenty years ago. In addition, phones give access to education: learners can use language apps, online courses and digital libraries wherever they are.

However, relying on smartphones also causes problems. Many people spend hours scrolling through social media, which can reduce their concentration and affect their sleep. There are also risks to privacy and security, because phones store a great deal of personal information that criminals may try to steal. Furthermore, some people feel anxious or lost when they cannot use their phone, which suggests an unhealthy level of dependence.

In my view, most of these disadvantages are caused by the way people use their phones rather than by the technology itself. Simple habits, such as switching off notifications, keeping phones out of the bedroom and using strong passwords, can reduce the risks considerably.

In conclusion, smartphones make daily life faster, easier and more connected. Although they can be harmful if used carelessly, I believe that the benefits clearly outweigh the drawbacks.

t2.p: Crime rates among young people are rising in some cities. What are the reasons for this, and what can be done about it?
t2.pv: Tội phạm trong giới trẻ tăng ở một số thành phố. Lý do là gì và có thể làm gì?
t2.m:
In some cities, young people are committing more crimes than they did in the past. This essay will explain the main reasons for this problem and suggest some measures that could help to solve it.

There are several reasons why young people may become involved in crime. The first is a lack of opportunities. In areas with high unemployment, teenagers who leave school without qualifications may feel that they have no future, and some turn to crime to earn money. The second reason is family problems. Children who grow up without enough attention or supervision from their parents are more likely to spend time on the streets and be influenced by older criminals. A third cause is peer pressure: young people often want to be accepted by a group, even if that group breaks the law.

To tackle this problem, action is needed in several areas. Firstly, governments should invest in education and training, so that young people have realistic chances of finding work. For example, apprenticeships that combine study with paid work can keep teenagers busy and give them useful skills. Secondly, local authorities could provide youth centres, sports clubs and music programmes, which offer safe places to spend free time. Finally, young offenders should receive support to change their behaviour, such as counselling and community service, rather than simply being sent to prison, where they may learn more about crime.

In conclusion, youth crime is mainly caused by a lack of opportunities, family problems and peer pressure. It can be reduced by better education, more activities for young people and rehabilitation instead of punishment alone.

t2.p: Some people believe that individuals can do little to protect the environment and that only governments and large companies can make a difference. Others think that every individual should take responsibility. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
t2.pv: Có người tin cá nhân làm được rất ít cho môi trường, chỉ nhà nước và doanh nghiệp lớn mới tạo khác biệt. Người khác cho rằng mỗi cá nhân phải có trách nhiệm. Bàn cả hai và nêu ý kiến.
t2.m:
Environmental problems such as climate change and pollution are among the most serious issues of our time. Some argue that ordinary citizens have little influence and that real change depends on the state and big business, while others insist that each of us must play a part. In my opinion, both groups have important roles to play.

On the one hand, it is true that the biggest changes depend on governments and businesses. A single person recycling plastic bottles has a tiny effect compared with a government that closes coal power stations or a company that changes how it produces goods. Governments can pass laws, introduce taxes on pollution and invest in public transport and renewable energy. Large companies control supply chains that affect millions of people. For example, if a major supermarket stops using plastic packaging, the effect is far greater than the efforts of thousands of individual shoppers.

On the other hand, individuals should not ignore their own responsibility. When millions of people change their habits, such as using public transport, eating less meat or wasting less food, the total effect becomes significant. Moreover, individuals are also voters and customers. Their choices at elections and in shops send a clear message to politicians and businesses, encouraging them to take environmental action.

In my view, the two approaches support each other. Governments and companies must lead with large-scale changes, but these changes are more likely to happen when ordinary people show that they care about the environment.

In conclusion, although governments and large companies have the greatest power, individual actions still matter, both directly and by influencing those in power.

t2.p: Nowadays, many people work from home rather than in an office. Why is this happening? Is it a positive or negative development?
t2.pv: Ngày nay nhiều người làm ở nhà thay vì văn phòng. Vì sao? Đây là thay đổi tích cực hay tiêu cực?
t2.m:
In recent years, a growing number of employees have started working from home instead of travelling to an office every day. This essay will explain why this trend is happening and argue that it is, on balance, a positive development.

There are several reasons for this change. The most important is technology. Fast internet connections, video-calling software and cloud storage mean that many office tasks can now be done from anywhere. The Covid-19 pandemic also played a major role, because it forced companies to try remote working on a large scale, and many discovered that it worked better than they expected. In addition, employers have realised that they can save money on office space if fewer staff come in each day.

I believe that this development is mainly positive. Working from home saves employees the time and cost of commuting, which can be several hours a week in large cities. This gives them more time for their families, exercise and rest. It can also reduce traffic and air pollution. For example, cities that saw many people working from home during the pandemic recorded noticeably cleaner air.

However, there are some disadvantages. Some people feel lonely and miss the social contact of the office, and it can be difficult to separate work from home life. Young employees may also learn less without colleagues around them. For these reasons, I think a mixed system, in which people work partly at home and partly in the office, is the best solution.

In conclusion, working from home has become common because of new technology and the experience of the pandemic. Although it has some drawbacks, I believe it is a positive development overall.
